title: Five-finger positions in C and G
summary: Learn finger numbers, then play in C and G positions with each hand separately.

lessons.title: Finger numbers
lessons.summary: Number your fingers 1 to 5 and play your first five-finger position.

steps.title: Numbering the fingers
steps.body:
Piano music numbers the fingers so fingering can be written above notes:

- **1** = thumb
- **2** = index
- **3** = middle
- **4** = ring
- **5** = little finger (pinky)

Both hands use the same numbers, so **both thumbs are 1**. In the right hand, 1 is on the left of the hand; in the left hand, 1 is on the right. Tap each finger on your leg while saying its number, both hands.

steps.title: C position, right hand
steps.body:
A **five-finger position** puts one finger on each of five neighboring white keys. In **right-hand C position**, finger 1 is on **middle C (C4)**, and fingers 2 to 5 rest on **D4 E4 F4 G4**.

Keep all five fingers resting on their keys, curved, even when they are not playing.

diagram.caption: Right hand C position: 1 on C4 … 5 on G4.

steps.title: Up and down the C position
steps.caption: C D E F G F E D C, one finger per key.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, C position: play fingers 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 1 (C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 F4 E4 D4 C4). One note per beat.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q w

mistakeTips: Keep every finger touching its key, even when not playing.
Finger 4 is the weakest; let it press with arm weight, not by squeezing.
Keep the thumb on its side corner, not flat.

questions.prompt: In right-hand C position, which finger plays F4?
In right-hand C position, which note is under finger 3?
questions.explanation: Finger 3 rests on the third key, E4.

reviewItems.prompt: Name the finger numbers from thumb to pinky.
reviewItems.answer: 1 thumb, 2 index, 3 middle, 4 ring, 5 pinky (same in both hands).

reviewItems.prompt: Right-hand C position: which finger is on G4?

lessons.title: Right hand: steps and skips
lessons.summary: Move by step and by skip in right-hand C position, and echo short phrases.

steps.title: Steps and skips
steps.body:
- A **step** moves to the next key and next finger: C to D, fingers 1 to 2.
- A **skip** jumps over one key: C to E, fingers 1 to 3. On the staff, a skip goes line to line or space to space.

In a five-finger position, the finger number tells you the note, so you rarely need to look down. Try to keep your eyes on the screen.

exercise.prompt: Skips: play 1 3 5 3 1 (C4 E4 G4 E4 C4), twice.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q h q q q q h

mistakeTips: Keep fingers 2 and 4 resting on D and F; do not lift them high.
Let your hand stay in place. Only the fingers move.

exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q h

mistakeTips: The skip from 3 back to 1 is E down to C.
Hold the last note for two beats.

exercise.prompt: Listen, then play the phrase back in right-hand C position.

mistakeTips: The phrase starts on C4 (finger 1).
Listen for steps (next key) versus skips (jumping one key).
Replay the phrase as often as you need.

questions.explanation: C to E jumps over D, so it is a skip.

questions.prompt: In right-hand C position, fingers 1–3–5 play…
On the staff, a skip moves from…
choices: A line to the next line
A line to the next space
A note to the same note
questions.explanation: Line to line (or space to space) skips one letter.

reviewItems.prompt: What is the difference between a step and a skip?
reviewItems.answer: A step goes to the next letter (next key); a skip jumps over one letter.

lessons.title: Left hand in C position
lessons.summary: Play the same five notes one octave lower with the left hand.

steps.title: Left-hand C position
steps.body:
Put your **left-hand finger 5 on C3** (the C below middle C). Fingers 4, 3, 2, 1 rest on **D3 E3 F3 G3**. The thumb ends up on G3.

Notice the reversal: going **up** the keyboard, the right hand counts 1→5 but the left hand counts **5→1**. This takes practice, so go slowly and say the numbers.

diagram.caption: Left hand C position: 5 on C3 … 1 on G3.

steps.title: Left hand up and down
steps.caption: C3 D3 E3 F3 G3 F3 E3 D3 C3.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, C position: fingers 5 4 3 2 1 2 3 4 5 (C3 D3 E3 F3 G3 F3 E3 D3 C3).
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q w

mistakeTips: Finger 5 on C3, not C4.
Keep the left wrist level; it tends to drop.
Fingers 4 and 5 are weaker in most people's left hand. Slow down rather than forcing.

exercise.prompt: Left-hand skips: 5 3 1 3 5 (C3 E3 G3 E3 C3), twice.
exercise.rhythm: q q q q h q q q q h

mistakeTips: Finger 3 on E3 sits in the middle of the position.
Let the hand rest on all five keys between notes.

questions.prompt: In left-hand C position, which finger is on C3?
questions.explanation: Left hand 5 on C3, thumb on G3.

questions.prompt: In left-hand C position, which note is under the thumb?
questions.explanation: The left thumb rests on G3.

questions.prompt: Going up the keyboard, the left-hand finger numbers go…
questions.explanation: The left thumb is on the right side of the hand, so finger numbers go down as notes go up.

reviewItems.prompt: Left-hand C position: where does finger 5 go?
reviewItems.answer: C3, the C below middle C.

lessons.title: G position, each hand
lessons.summary: Move both hands to G position and play the same patterns starting on G.

steps.title: G position
steps.body:
Positions are named after the note under the lowest finger.

- **Right hand G position:** finger 1 on **G4** (the G above middle C); fingers 2 to 5 on **A4 B4 C5 D5**.
- **Left hand G position:** finger 5 on **G2** (the second G below middle C); fingers 4 to 1 on **A2 B2 C3 D3**.

All five keys are white, just as in C position. The finger patterns you learned work the same way here; only the starting note changes.

diagram.caption: Right hand G position: 1 on G4 … 5 on D5.

steps.title: Left hand G position
steps.body: G2 is lower than anything you have played so far. Play it with firm arm weight so it sounds clearly. Low notes are a little harder for a phone microphone to hear; if a note is marked uncertain, play it slightly louder.

diagram.caption: Left hand G position: 5 on G2 … 1 on D3.

exercise.prompt: Right hand, G position: 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 1 (G4 A4 B4 C5 D5 C5 B4 A4 G4).
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q w

mistakeTips: Finger 1 on the G just above middle C.
Finger 4 is on C5, one octave above middle C.
Keep the fingers curved and resting on their keys.

exercise.prompt: Left hand, G position: 5 4 3 2 1 2 3 4 5 (G2 A2 B2 C3 D3 C3 B2 A2 G2).
exercise.rhythm: q q q q q q q q w

mistakeTips: G2 is two Gs below middle C.
The thumb lands on D3.
Play low notes with full arm weight so the microphone can hear them.

exercise.prompt: Right-hand skips in G: 1 3 5 3 1 (G4 B4 D5 B4 G4).

mistakeTips: Fingers 1–3–5 in G position play G B D.

questions.prompt: Right-hand G position: which note is under finger 1?
questions.explanation: Right thumb on the G above middle C.

questions.prompt: Left-hand G position: which finger plays G2?
Fingers 1–3–5 in right-hand G position play…
Why can the same finger patterns work in C and G position?
choices: Both positions cover five neighboring white keys
C and G are the same note
questions.explanation: Both positions sit on five neighboring white keys, so the fingers move the same way.

reviewItems.prompt: Right-hand G position covers which notes?
Play the note under right-hand finger 5 in G position.

steps.caption: Right hand C position. Finger 3 on the first note (E4). The melody only moves by step, except for the repeated notes.

reviewItems.prompt: What does transposing a melody mean?
reviewItems.answer: Playing it starting on a different note, keeping the same pattern of steps.
